content.thinking:
I need to write the postmortem without embedding any actual figures, replacing specific times, durations, and numbers with placeholders like {duration} or {began}, while keeping descriptive labels. I'm working through the causal chain starting with the symptom of failed account page requests and the associated error rate.

Tracing the sequence: the division-by-zero error in the spend summary code only triggered because the monthly-spend rollout flag was switched on, and that rollout appears to have gone from no traffic to full traffic almost immediately without staged gating — a likely contributing factor alongside the apparent absence of a test for the zero-denominator case, though I should be careful since that's inferred rather than confirmed. For action items, I'm keeping the existing code-fix task and considering new ones around staged rollouts with error-rate gating and adding the missing test, while also noting the detection delay between when the warning logs started and when the alert actually fired.

Looking at the recovery, the service returned to baseline right around when the flag was reverted, which lines up well enough to attribute the fix confidently. I also notice the flag change itself wasn't captured in the production change feed as a tracked deploy, which could point to another gap worth flagging as an action item, though I want to keep the list focused rather than sprawling. For the executive summary, I'm avoiding stating specific figures and being careful with how I phrase things.

action_items.item: Roll out feature flags in stages (for example a small share of traffic first), with an automatic rollback when the error rate on the affected path rises.
Add a test for the spend summary code that covers a zero divisor and other empty-data inputs, and require it in the proposed fix before the flag is re-enabled.

Alert on a sustained rise in account page errors or on the ZeroDivisionError log signature, tuned to fire within a minute or two of onset. Also feed flag changes into the change-event history that the Investigator reads, so flag toggles show up next to deploys.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers saw account page requests fail. The error rate rose from {errors_before} to {errors_while_broken} on average and {errors_at_worst} at worst over {duration}, and the HighErrorRate alert paged.

The failing requests were raising a ZeroDivisionError (division by zero) in the spend summary module on the account page path. Latency, CPU and memory stayed flat, so this was a logic error and not a resource or traffic problem.

That code path started running because the feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on. The flag evaluations moved from almost all off to all on within a minute or so, and the errors began in lockstep with that.

The new spend summary code does not handle a zero divisor, and nothing limited the flag's exposure before it reached all traffic. The record does not say what value was zero or why. The proposed fix is meant to address the defect itself.
Reverting the flag to off stopped the failures. The service was back at baseline from {recovered} and the paging rule stopped firing.

contributing_factors.factor: The flag was ramped to full traffic almost at once, with no staged rollout or automatic error-rate check, so a defect in the flagged code reached most shoppers before anyone could react.
The flagged code path apparently had no test for the zero-divisor case, and the defect was not caught before the flag went on. This is inferred from the failure and not directly shown in the record.

Detection was slow. The alert was raised at {alert_raised}, several minutes after the onset at {began}, even though error-rate warnings and ZeroDivisionError lines had been logged earlier. The change feed showed no production changes, because the flag change was not recorded as one.

input.executive_summary: For about {duration}, from {began} until {recovered}, a large share of shoppers' account page requests failed. The error rate rose from {errors_before} to an average of {errors_while_broken} and peaked at {errors_at_worst}. A new feature, the monthly spend summary, had been switched on and contained a bug that crashed the page when it ran. Argus identified the feature flag as the cause and switched it off. The service returned to baseline and the alert stopped firing. A draft pull request with a code fix has been proposed and is awaiting review. Until it is merged, the flag must stay off.

got_lucky: The failure was limited to the account page, and the flag could be reverted instantly without a deploy. A defect in code that could not be switched off would have lasted longer.
went_well: Argus formed the right candidate within seconds of picking up the alert and tied the flag change to the error logs.
Reverting the flag was a quick, low-risk mitigation. The metrics confirmed recovery and the paging rule stopped firing.
A draft fix pull request was proposed automatically right after mitigation.
went_wrong: The flag was exposed to all traffic with no staged rollout, and the defect hit a large share of account page requests.
The alert fired several minutes after the onset, and the change-event query returned no changes because the flag toggle was not recorded as one.

input.root_cause: Turning on the feature flag monthly-spend-feature sent account page requests down a code path in the spend summary module that divides by zero (ZeroDivisionError). The flag was ramped to all traffic within about a minute, so a large share of account page requests failed until the flag was turned off.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for many shoppers
